attributes.probed_form:
RAW BASELINE real 58, insns T75/O75, opcode multiset DIFFERS: target-only +1 mr, ours-only -1 li. Residual is three clusters: an `lwz` displacement move at +0x6c/+0x70, and the form site at +0x84 where ours decodes ('li',23,0) -- materialise the constant 0 -- and the target ('copy',24,22) -- copy a register that already holds 0.
AXIS FAMILY 1, scoped pragmas around this function alone:
  `#pragma opt_lifetimes off`/`reset` -> NEUTRAL, real 58 unchanged.
  `#pragma opt_propagation off`/`reset` -> NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, object bytes unchanged.
  `#pragma opt_common_subs off`/`reset` -> REGRESSED real 58->89 and grew the function (insns T75/O76, multiset 5t). This is the informative one: constant/expression reuse is exactly the machinery behind a known-zero register being copied instead of rematerialised, and disabling it moves the function firmly the WRONG way, so our build is already on the reuse-favouring side of that decision.
AXIS FAMILY 2, declaration order over the six-line block `u8 unused[8]; s32 channel = 0; s32 channelMask; s32 infoOffset; s32 i; s32 adjustment;` -- 11 orderings compiled and scored. identity (58) is the global minimum; moving `i` or `adjustment` to the front costs 66/70 and moving `infoOffset`/`i` to the back costs 70. Already optimal.
